t: This is the site of the Serpentine Gallery Pavilion for 2008, a temporary building that has since been taken down, so what you see now is only the setting. It was designed by Frank Gehry, the Canadian-American architect known for sculptural, often undulating buildings in materials like titanium and stainless steel. His best-known works include the Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao, the Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles and the Louis Vuitton Foundation in Paris. This pavilion was his contribution to the gallery's series of summer structures.
